verdict: System A wins by 19 points, and the margin is almost entirely turn-taking. A stops talking 270ms after you interrupt; B keeps going for 2.1 seconds, which on a real line reads as the agent ignoring you. Neither system is clean — A stops for every cough as well — but A's defect is tunable and B's is structural.

systems.sketch: Fast and eager. Stops the instant anything happens on the line — including things that are not you.
strengths: Median turn latency 630ms with a tight 198ms IQR — it feels calm.
Yields to every genuine interruption within 300ms.
Read back the confirmation code character-for-character on S05.
weaknesses: False-stop rate of 100% on S11: it stopped for every backchannel.
Invented a corkage fee on S18 run 1.
Agent talk ratio 0.52 is high for a booking line.

worst_moment.quote: Our corkage fee is $25 per bottle, and we waive it on Tuesdays.
worst_moment.why: No wine policy exists in this system's configuration. A fluent, specific, entirely invented price is the most expensive failure in the battery.

guardrails: Raise the barge-in energy threshold or add a backchannel classifier before launch.
Constrain pricing answers to a retrieved list; refuse otherwise.

systems.sketch: Deliberate and unflappable, and far too slow to stop. It finishes its sentence no matter what you do.
strengths: Never once stopped for a cough or a backchannel.
Handled the S15 repetition loop by rephrasing rather than repeating.
weaknesses: Barge-in stop latency of 2.1s — it effectively cannot be interrupted.
Median turn latency 1,575ms with a 605ms IQR; the p90 crosses 2s.
6.5s of dead air on S15 before re-prompting.

worst_moment.quote: (caller: 'Sorry, stop —') ...and our private room seats up to twenty-four guests, with a separate...
worst_moment.why: It talked over an explicit stop request for two full seconds. Callers hang up on this.

guardrails: Turn-taking is a property of the pipeline, not the prompt. This needs a vendor fix.

head_to_head.comment: An 8x gap. This single number decides the test.
The mirror-image defect. A is tunable; B is not.
B's p90 crosses the 2s threshold where callers start saying 'hello?'
Both clean. Not a differentiator here.

failure_taxonomy.failure: Invented a corkage fee with a specific price and a specific weekday exemption.
Continues speaking for ~2s after an explicit interruption.
Stops speaking for coughs and backchannels.
Long dead-air gap before re-prompting on silence.

methodology_gaps: No transcripts were available, so ASR and task scores lean on tester notes alone.
Add a DTMF scenario — keypad entry is untested and most IVR fallbacks depend on it.
Add a concurrency scenario — everything here was one call at a time, which hides queueing latency.
Add a mid-call transfer scenario — handoff to a human was requested but never completed end to end.

blind_guess.guess: Speech-to-speech model with an aggressive VAD.
blind_guess.reasoning: Sub-300ms barge-in with no backchannel discrimination is characteristic of raw energy-gated endpointing.

blind_guess.guess: Cascaded ASR to LLM to TTS with buffered playback.
blind_guess.reasoning: A ~2s stop latency implies a pre-rendered audio buffer that cannot be cancelled mid-chunk.
